analysis.title: GS Sheren - Five Asian Charts to Watch 1 Nov 2026
key_insights: China tech fell about 23% in a month, but the Greater China Macro Risk Basket is at a one-year low. Sheren reads this as not a systemic China-risk event.
Pressure is increasingly tied to the broader AI-capex reset, driven by concerns over hyperscaler debt, financing costs and monetization that have challenged the former AI winners globally.

Directional positioning is the lightest of the year. Sheren sees the unwind moving from acceleration toward exhaustion and calls the October correction an increasingly attractive entry point into Asia.

Foreign and hedge fund de-risking in October was offset by domestic buying concentrated in the former AI winners. EM Asia ex-China saw US$50.5bn of foreign outflows, led by Taiwan (US$31.8bn) and Korea (US$14.6bn).
Hedge fund Asia net allocation fell from 30.2% to 27.3%. Net leverage for Asia Fundamental L/S managers dropped 16.9pts to 48%.

In the final week, Sean Navin reported the lightest APAC directional skew of the year, and foreign investors returned to Korea for the first time in 11 weeks. Sheren says this is not yet a reversal, since China AI hardware is still deleveraging.

The Nasdaq 100 lost more than $3 trillion over the month. Japan, Korea and Taiwan lost more than $1.3 trillion of market cap in October as earnings sharpened doubts over whether AI revenue will arrive fast enough to justify the spend.

Hyperscaler AI capex is increasingly outpacing internally generated cash flow, which forces more reliance on bonds, leases and structured financing while credit spreads widen. The concern is financing capacity and cost rather than near-term solvency.

AI hyperscaler debt issuance through 2027 could equal roughly 30% of expected U.S. Treasury issuance. Sheren says this diversion of capital into tech corporate bonds is forcing the Treasury to raise its yields to attract buyers.

The debate has moved from capex durability to value capture and financing capacity. Capex consumed roughly 30% of hyperscaler sales in Q2 2026, free cash flow has collapsed even as earnings compounded, and HY AI credit trades 213 bps wide of HY ex-AI.

GIR expects AI investment as a share of GDP to rise more slowly over the next year. Together with the fading boost from last year's US depreciation allowances, this will weigh on capital spending growth, especially in the US.
About 475 companies (41% of MSCI EM companies, ~50% of market cap) have reported 3Q results. 3Q EPS is tracking at 56% YoY versus 72% at the start of the season, with a median surprise of -1%.

EM sales beats (34%) exceeded misses (24%), but earnings beats were scarce (33% beats vs 45% misses). North Asia and China had larger negative surprises and downgrades, India and MENA were relatively robust, and Tech was weak against strength in Utilities and Real Estate.

The CSI 300 entered bear-market territory, led by technology. Margin balances fell below RMB2.4tn, and Southbound investors sold for a 14th consecutive session, taking October outflows to roughly HK$24bn.

China manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 and non-manufacturing PMI to 49.7. Sheren attributes the sell-off to weaker fundamentals, crowded positioning and deleveraging rather than rising systemic China risk.
